sn2.10:1.2: Then at that time the Sun god was seized by the asura lord Rāhu.
sn2.10:1.3: Then the Sun god, recollecting the Fortunate One, on that occasion recited this verse:
sn2.10:2.2: you who are free in every way!
sn2.10:2.4: therefore please be a refuge to me.”
sn2.10:3.1: Then, with reference to the Sun god, the Fortunate One addressed the asura lord Rāhu with a verse:
sn2.10:4.1: “To the Realised One, the Worthy One,
sn2.10:4.2: the Sun has gone for refuge,
sn2.10:4.3: you must release the Sun, Rāhu!
sn2.10:5.1: He who, in complete darkness, is a light-maker,
sn2.10:5.2: who is brilliant, a great circle of fire,
sn2.10:5.3: do not devour he who roams the sky, Rāhu!
sn2.10:5.4: Release the Sun, who is my kinsman, Rāhu!”
sn2.10:6.1: Then the asura lord Rāhu, having released the Sun god, hurriedly approached the asura lord Vepacitti, and after approaching, anxious, and horrified, he stood on one side.
sn2.10:6.2: While he was standing on one side the asura lord Vepacitti recited this verse to the asura lord Rāhu:
sn2.10:7.4: why do you stand (there) like someone anxious and frightened?”
sn2.10:8.2: while living I will have no happiness,
sn2.10:8.3: - I am one to whom the Buddha has chanted a verse
sn2.10:8.4: if I do not release the Sun.”
